discovery_queries.purpose: Exhaustive direct-mention inventory; false positives with the male name Khudayj are retained and classified.

entry_targets.name: Hakim ibn Hizam
entry_targets.reason: Nephew and purchaser of Zayd for Khadijah; the entry supplies his direct household and trade connection.

entry_targets.name: Khuzayma ibn Hakim al-Sulami
entry_targets.reason: A weak but explicit report places him in Khadijah's caravan with Muhammad before the marriage; retained with Ibn Hajar's criticism.

entry_targets.name: Zuhayr ibn Qunfudh
entry_targets.reason: His report places Khadijah meeting Muhammad at the valley mosque during the Hira period.

entry_targets.name: Zayd ibn Haritha
entry_targets.reason: Khadijah's household acquired Zayd and she gave him to Muhammad; his entry preserves the adoption and earliest-belief history.

entry_targets.name: al-Tahir (Abd Allah), son of Muhammad
entry_targets.reason: Direct child entry preserving conflicting enumerations and names of Khadijah's sons.

entry_targets.name: Afif al-Kindi
entry_targets.reason: Eyewitness report of Muhammad, Ali, and Khadijah praying together at the beginning of Islam.

entry_targets.name: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad
entry_targets.reason: Direct child entry, including disputed age at death and Khadijah's grief.

entry_targets.name: Maysara
entry_targets.reason: Khadijah's servant and Muhammad's companion on her caravan before their marriage.

entry_targets.name: Nabbash ibn Zurara
entry_targets.reason: One identification of Abu Hala, Khadijah's earlier husband; Ibn Hajar explicitly disputes his companionship.

entry_targets.name: Nabbash ibn Zurara (duplicate Abu Hala entry)
entry_targets.reason: A second, explicitly erroneous Abu Hala identification needed to preserve the name conflict.

entry_targets.name: Nastur the monk
entry_targets.reason: The caravan omen report attributed to Maysara and tied to Khadijah's decision to marry Muhammad.

entry_targets.name: Hala ibn Abi Hala
entry_targets.reason: A disputed prior-household child whose entry records confusion with Khadijah's sister Hala.

entry_targets.name: Hind ibn Abi Hala
entry_targets.reason: Khadijah's son and Muhammad's stepson; the entry also preserves competing names for Abu Hala.

entry_targets.name: Waraqa ibn Nawfal
entry_targets.reason: Khadijah's cousin and principal witness-interpreter in the first-revelation account.

entry_targets.name: Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi
entry_targets.reason: Khadijah's nephew and Zaynab's husband; his entry preserves the necklace and household continuity after Khadijah's death.

9151: مات قبل أن يدعو بحيرا رسول الله الناس إلى الإسلام

include: Every passage that directly concerns Khadijah's life, household, marriage, trade, first-belief role, death, or remembered character.
The complete al-Isabah entry of an immediate associate when that entry adds material context to one of those events.
Conflicting genealogical, chronological, or naming evidence needed to understand the canonical account.
exclude: A bare kinship reference that adds no fact about Khadijah or the relevant associate.
A false positive for the distinct male name Khudayj or another Khadijah.
Generic transmitters, later historians, and cited book authors who are not actors in the narrative.
selection_policy.uncertain: Retain as pending with evidence; never silently discard it.

fill_contract.source_locator: Usul result id plus volume, printed page, reader index, and canonical text hash
fill_contract.incremental_rule: A later cohort or full-volume run may add entries and mentions without rewriting reviewed entries.
fill_contract.review_rule: Autonomous translation, criticism, witness comparison, adjudication, and deterministic QA precede human review.
